key_insight: Adaptive 'elastic' context management keeps different parts of an agent's trajectory at different levels of detail according to relevance, preventing context bloat while preserving information needed for long-horizon search and reasoning.
problem_solved: Long-horizon search agents accumulate ever-growing intermediate content that increases compute/cost and the risk of errors; the paper addresses how to manage that working context efficiently and adaptively.
method: Introduce Context-ReAct: organize an agent's trajectory into multi-resolution tiers (detailed, summarized, compressed/archive) and move segments between tiers based on their current relevance.
Use a dynamic relevance scorer and cost-aware controller to decide when to summarize, compress, archive, or rehydrate segments so the agent keeps only what matters at the needed fidelity.
Integrate selective retrieval and rehydration into the agent loop and tool calls so reasoning remains accurate without replaying the full raw context.
impact: Makes long-horizon search agents more scalable and cost-effective by reducing memory and compute overhead while lowering error rates from overloaded context, enabling longer, cheaper, and more reliable agent workflows for ML practitioners.

paper_title: LongSeeker: Elastic Context Orchestration for Long-Horizon Search Agents
paper_authors: Yijun Lu, Rui Ye, Yuwen Du, Jiajun Wang, Songhua Liu
